Specific_Friction: Growing teams with no standardized processes face a knowledge transfer collapse when employees leave — all institutional knowledge walks out the door with them. 'We didn't know the mechanics of how they got their specific tasks accomplished — we just knew that they did.' New hires have no roadmap, no playbook, no way to replicate what predecessors built. Every person develops their own communication style and tool preferences, creating a patchwork that makes cross-team coordination impossible and makes scaling operations a constant firefight instead of a repeatable system.
Severity/Impact: High. Project management scaling at university career center. Named exec: Michael Turner (Associate Director, Center for Career Exploration and Success), Miami University. Quantified: 200+ annual virtual and in-person events organized by a 25-member team; knowledge repository built; event details (presenter contacts, attendee feedback, budgets, marketing images) stored historically; campus reach increased. Quote: 'When teammates left, we didn't know the mechanics of how they got their specific tasks accomplished — we just knew that they did. This left our new employees without a roadmap or even a playbook training them how to read it.'

Specific_Friction: Companies scaling from departmental size to cross-team operations without standardized project management face a compounding coordination crisis: every new hire multiplies the communication complexity, email threads become unreadable, meetings multiply to cover what should be in a shared doc, and 'no source of truth for past, present and future projects' means everyone operates on different data. When knowledge lives in people's heads and in email threads rather than in a shared system, operational memory is literally walking out the door every time someone resigns — and onboarding new people means starting from zero every time.
Severity/Impact: Critical. Project management transformation at retail chain. Named exec: Molly Quella (Project Manager, Store Planning), Lids. Quantified: 100+ hours saved across teams; 66% meeting efficiency improvement; email from 100+ to under 50 after a 3-day weekend; 25 stores under construction, 3 rollouts ongoing, 50 more opening in 2024; 135 employees on platform; vendor bid tracking in platform; manual inventory counting eliminated. Quote: 'We had no source of truth for past, present and future projects. This was problematic because when someone leaves a company, all of their knowledge leaves with them.'
